global_rules: Calendar substitutions apply everywhere, including source success signals: May 12/13/14 2027 mean calendar.day_1/day_2/day_3; April 1 means confirmation_due/biography_due; April 14 means headshot_due; April 15 means release_due; May 1 means slides_due. Event names containing 2027 remain stable labels, not calendar instructions. Existing-event fallback creation in source prose is superseded by canonical event binding.
Run only on an explicitly authorized disposable UAT target. This pack does not authorize resets, deployments, paid model runs, or messages to real recipients.

Before executing, fill the persona-to-account table in the result context with observed account IDs, emails, display names and role. Never store passwords, cookies, magic-link tokens, or private asset URLs in results.

Fixture names are semantic aliases. Substitute the mapped account consistently in signup/login, invites, CSV import, search, assertions and recipient checks. Snapshot passwords and conflicting snapshot email addresses are never execution credentials.

Record the organization UUID and primary event UUID when created. Subsequent steps must navigate to that exact event; do not identify a target by title alone or silently create a replacement. CFP-S1 step 12 uses a separate recorded secondary event UUID and must leave the primary event intact.

Gate chained scenarios on the preceding scenario's evidenced handoff. Missing upstream records block dependent steps; do not fabricate them through APIs or database writes. An optional unsupported feature may fail its rubric without blocking a handoff whose required records were genuinely created.

Within each step record the account actually used, event UUID or explicit no-event scope, result, failure class when applicable, observations and safe evidence references. Persona switches in the original steps remain mandatory.

Keep all original pass criteria. Corrections change execution identity, scheduling or safe sequencing, not the product bar. A workaround is not a pass. Record unsupported features as failures or evidenced absences exactly as the criterion permits.

Execute every manual_instructions block, including conditional blocks on auto criteria. Record not_applicable only with evidence that the source condition is false; never use it for an unavailable required feature.

Use the supplied materialization command to generate an isolated run packet with resolved fixture identities, CSV rows and relative review dates. Retain the original read-only snapshot for comparison.

acceptance_checks.name: Time-zone preview, update and persistence
steps: After AIA-S2 has published an agenda, capture the canonical event zone, each agenda item's local date/start/end, CFP and review deadline UTC instants, and current audit entries. Missing agenda or deadline records block this check. Record IDs and sanitized evidence, not private form content.

Preview changing America/Los_Angeles to Asia/Kolkata without applying. The confirmation must explicitly list both effects: agenda wall-clock dates/times are preserved (their UTC instants change), while CFP/review deadline UTC instants are unchanged (their local display may change). Capture before/after values per surface and confirm preview itself made no persisted changes.

Apply the fresh preview, reload the editor, public CFP and published agenda. Every agenda item keeps its local date/start/end under the new zone; every CFP/review deadline keeps its exact UTC instant. Verify confirmation agrees with persistence and public rendering. Capture exactly one successful time-zone-change audit event for this operation, not one per item.

Preview a reverse change, then edit one agenda item through supported UI in another browser context. Applying the earlier preview digest must return HTTP 409 and leave zone, agenda and deadlines unchanged from immediately before that rejected apply. Obtain a new preview before retrying; capture sanitized request status and affected values.

Exercise the conflict rejection with an explicitly recorded conflicting fixture through supported UI (a time-zone conversion conflict, not merely a stale digest). Preview/apply must report the conflict and applying must return HTTP 409, with no partial zone, agenda or deadline writes and no successful-change audit event. If the UI cannot construct a conflict or expose apply, mark this step blocked with the missing prerequisite; never claim conflict safety from the stale-digest test alone.

Restore the original agenda item values and America/Los_Angeles using a fresh preview. Verify editor, public agenda, public CFP and review deadlines against the baseline. Record restoration separately from the single successful update being counted above. Missing preview, wrong semantics or missing confirmation is a product failure, not an assumed pass.

acceptance_checks.name: Canonical track IDs and fail-closed embeds
steps: Publish approved sessions on two tracks in the canonical event and obtain their track UUIDs from supported UI/network responses. Generate a track-filtered embed. Inspect all five generated outputs individually: iframe, Basic HTML link, JSON feed, XML feed and iCal calendar feed. Each must carry the same canonical track_id parameter; record the URL or snippet and filtered result for each. Verify only selected-track published sessions and eligible speakers appear.

Rename that track without changing its UUID, reload the same embed URL and verify selection still follows the ID. Exercise a second track with a colliding display name if the product permits it; names must not widen ID selection.

Replace track_id with an unknown UUID, then one belonging to the secondary event, across all five outputs. JSON must include matched:false in its filter envelope and no sessions/speakers; other outputs must fail closed without an unfiltered list or cross-event data. Record each response, not only a screenshot of one widget.

Inspect the public_speakers response for selected and unmatched track requests: Cache-Control must include no-store and results must stay track-scoped. Record sanitized header evidence without cookies or authorization headers.

Save the embed and inspect its registry row: it must show the selected track, not just an unqualified event embed. Clear the filter deliberately and prove an unfiltered request is distinct. Restore the track name and temporary edits.

acceptance_checks.name: Scorecard type switching and saved semantics
steps: Create a draft scorecard with Score weights 40, 35 and 25. Confirm the displayed total is 100; change the first weight to 10 and confirm 70 immediately.

Switch the second criterion to Text and confirm 35. Switch the first to Select and the third to Text; confirm No Score criteria and absence of stale numeric weight controls. Switch a criterion back to Score and verify appropriate required numeric constraints return.

On a separate draft card, enter weight 0 on a Score criterion, switch that criterion to Free text, then save. Saving must succeed and the submitted/persisted weight must be null, not zero or an omitted validation error. Capture sanitized payload and reload evidence; do not accept a successful toast alone.

Before saving another draft, set a Score weight to 35, switch to Free text, then switch back to Score: the weight control must restore draft value 35. Repeat with 0: switching back must restore 0 and Score validation must reject it; switching to Free text again must allow save with null. Do not conflate preservation of an unsaved draft with restoring an old numeric value after reloading a saved Free text field.

Configure a valid mixed Score/Select/Text card, save and reload. Verify field types, options and score weights persist. Open the assigned reviewer form and verify each type renders and submits correctly; non-Score fields must not contribute stale weights. Do not alter finalized evaluations.
